title: Ἄνδρες ⟨δύο περὶ θεῶν ἐρίζοντες⟩
titleEn: Two Men Quarrelling about the Gods
part: Two Men Quarrelling about the Gods (Chambry 44)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 44. Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« », ⟨ ⟩ for editorial supplements). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ἄνδρες δύο ἐμάχοντο τίνες τῶν θεῶν μείζους, Θησεὺς ἢ Ἡρακλῆς.
sentences.tr: Andres dyo emachonto tines tōn theōn meizous, Thēseus ē Hēraklēs.
sentences.l: Two men were fighting over which of the gods were greater, Theseus or Heracles.
sentences.n: ἐμάχοντο takes an indirect question with nothing to introduce it: 'they were fighting (over) which…'. Theseus and Heracles are heroes who received cult as gods, each with his own devoted region. The angle brackets in Chambry's title, ⟨δύο περὶ θεῶν ἐρίζοντες⟩, mark words the editor supplies; the manuscripts give only Ἄνδρες.

sentences.t: Οἱ δὲ θεοὶ ὀργισθέντες αὐτοῖς ἑκάτερος τὴν ἑτέρου χώραν ἠμύνατο.
sentences.tr: Hoi de theoi orgisthentes autois hekateros tēn heterou chōran ēmynato.
sentences.l: And the gods, having-become-angry at them, each took-vengeance-on the country of the other.
sentences.n: ἠμύνατο is the middle of ἀμύνω: the active is 'ward off', the middle with the accusative 'requite, take vengeance on'. ἑκάτερος, 'each of the two', is singular though it stands in apposition to the plural θεοί — Greek regularly picks a pair apart this way. τὴν ἑτέρου χώραν is 'the other one's country'; which country that is stays compressed. Taken plainly it is the rival god's own territory, so that each god punished the region devoted to the other. The Greek does not settle it.

sentences.t: Ὅτι τῶν ὑπεξουσίων ἡ ἔρις τοὺς δεσπότας πείθει ὀργίλους εἶναι κατὰ τῶν ὑπηκόων.
sentences.tr: Hoti tōn hypexousiōn hē eris tous despotas peithei orgilous einai kata tōn hypēkoōn.
sentences.l: That the strife of those-under-authority persuades the masters to be quick-tempered against their subjects.
sentences.i: That when dependants quarrel, it moves their masters to turn an angry temper on those under them.
sentences.n: A bare Ὅτι moral: the 'the story shows' is unexpressed in the Greek, which begins simply 'That…'. ὑπεξούσιοι are people who stand under another's power — dependants, servants, subordinates.
